title: Kuperberg coset sieve: subexponential DCP with time growth index 1/2

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the Kuperberg coset sieve of proof.md (reduction of each source copy to a labelled phase qubit via QFT_N, collimation over L = ceil(sqrt(n)) blocks, and majority-vote secret reconstruction, n = ceil(log2 N)) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 2/3 on every execution branch, and has worst-case total work T(N,s) = 2^{O(sqrt(n))}, i.e. the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = 2^{sqrt(n)}. All hidden constants are absolute. The growth index of this envelope is exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the two workspace bounds and the sample bound below, for the one algorithm and parameter choice L = ceil(sqrt(n)).

For the same Kuperberg coset sieve and configuration L = ceil(sqrt(n)) in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = 2^{O(sqrt(n))} bits (the pool of at most 2^{O(sqrt(n))} n-bit labels and recorded combination bits plus O(n^2) arithmetic scratch), with n = ceil(log2 N) and absolute constants. Its envelope B_C(n) = 2^{sqrt(n)} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time and quantum-workspace bounds, the sample bound, and full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg coset sieve and configuration L = ceil(sqrt(n)) in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, worst-case peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = 2^{O(sqrt(n))} qubits (at most 2^{O(sqrt(n))} simultaneously live phase qubits in a collimation stage plus O(n^2) ancillas for QFT_N and the combination gates), with n = ceil(log2 N) and absolute constants. Its envelope B_Q(n) = 2^{sqrt(n)} has growth index exactly 1/2. This holds jointly with the stated time and classical-workspace bounds, the sample bound, and full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg coset sieve and configuration L = ceil(sqrt(n)) in proof.md, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh DCP source copies acquired on every execution branch, including every discarded combination outcome, discarded zero label, and failed or restarted run, is 2^{O(sqrt(n))}. The uniform bit-length envelope B_samples(n) = 2^{sqrt(n)} has growth index exactly 1/2. Each acquired copy incurs the model's n+1 work cost. This holds jointly with the stated total-work and workspace bounds and unconditional full-secret success probability at least 2/3.

For the same Kuperberg coset sieve and configuration L = ceil(sqrt(n)) in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
